messages:
sophie: Heads up — canary deploy (v2.14.1) to prod is failing on startup for the encoder service. Seeing repeated crashloops in the canary pods. Logs show a config parse error referencing /etc/encoder/config.yaml

oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered for severity P2: encoder-canary-startup-failure — paging oncall@rotation (sarah).

mike: I'm looking. logs from pod-enc-2: `error: invalid value at line 3: 'timeout' expected int but got '10s'` — looks like config schema change in 2.14.1.

alex: That sounds like the new config schema landed in the image but the configMap applied during rollout uses the old format. Did the helm chart bump the encoder config?

jamie: Confirmed — CI pipeline templated `encoder.timeout: "10s"` as a string due to the new helmv3 template change. Should be `10` (seconds).

sophie: Can we kill the canary rollout and rollback to 2.14.0? We need to stop new pods spinning and avoid HPA thrash.

mike: Initiating rollback now. `kubectl rollout undo deployment/encoder -n prod --to-revision=3`

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Rollback started for deployment encoder in prod (requested by mike). Watching rollout status...

jamie: Also patching the ConfigMap to a quick fix (convert timeout to int) to avoid future bad images, but we should still rollback images.

alex: Patch applied: `kubectl patch configmap encoder-config -n prod --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/data/timeout","value":"10"}]'` — verifying pods.

sophie: Customer impact check: mid-PDT we saw ~3% elevated 502s on the inference endpoint, primarily EU region. CS flagged two customers with increased error rate. No data loss.

mike: HPA note — during the crashloops HPA attempted to scale up because liveness probes failed then CPU spiked on remaining replicas — we had a transient node pressure event during the canary because of rapid restarts.

jamie: Paging SRE to monitor node eviction events — `kubectl get events -n prod --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | tail -n 50` shows kubelet OOM score adjustments and transient kube-proxy restarts on node-ip-07.

oncall-bot: oncall-handoff: sarah is currently on rotation and has acknowledged the pager.

sarah: I'm on it. Taking ownership of the incident. Current plan: 1) finish rollback 2) ensure configmap fixed 3) monitor HPA and node stability 4) postmortem if customers affected.

sophie: Thanks. Also enable feature-flag kill-switch for encoder-v2 rollout to block future auto-promote: `ffctl disable rollout/encoder-v2` — prevents accidental retriggers.

ops-bot: feature-flag: rollout/encoder-v2 disabled (requested by sophie).

mike: Rollback completed, new replicaset stabilized at 2.14.0. Pod counts back to desired.

jamie: ConfigMap patch verified, pods now boot cleanly. No more crashloops on canary.

sarah: Monitoring metrics: error rate back to baseline within 6 minutes post-rollback. HPA stabilized, no further node evictions. Will keep watch for 30m.

alex: Can we capture exact customer impact window for CS? When did 502s spike and when did they return?

sarah: Grafana window: spike started 2026-03-17T15:03:00Z, peaked 15:07, returned 15:12. Estimated affected requests: ~0.6% of total traffic, primarily EU cluster.

mike: Logging note: add a validation step in the pipeline to catch typed config fields. Simple JSON schema or helm unit test would have caught string vs int.

jamie: I'll open a quick ticket for a pre-deploy config lint step. Also adding a canary preflight that validates pod startup logs for < 1 crashloop in first 2 min.

sophie: Assign follow-ups: jamie for pipeline lint, mike for release checklist update, alex for postmortem draft. Sarah — please run the customer impact blurb for CS and link the metrics.

sarah: Will draft the incident blurb and post to #customer-impact. Will include timeline and which customers to notify if needed.

ops-bot: incident-bot: Incident resolved (encoder-canary-startup-failure). Severity lowered to INFO. Please file postmortem within 72h.

mike: Thanks everyone. Re-enabling rollout/encoder-v2 only after schema fix and a patch release. :thumbsup:
